extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientific community), including prospective candidates for St John's College Minor Scholarships/Exhibitions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria governing the Minor Scholarships and a 50-pound Exhibition at St John's College, Cambridge: eligibility, subjects examinable, procedural requirements, and tenure/conditions of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Minor Scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minor Scholarships are open to all persons under twenty years of age, whether students in the University or not, who have not yet commenced residence in the University or who are in the first term of their residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Minor Scholarship is tenable for two years, or until the scholar is elected to one of the Foundation Scholarships. It is understood that minor scholars or exhibitioners may be candidates for Sizarships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition (50 pounds per annum) purpose and conditional tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: An Exhibition of 50l. per annum is offered for proficiency in Natural Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exhibition is tenable for three years in case the Exhibitioner have passed within two years the previous examination as required for candidates for honours; otherwise the Exhibition to cease at the end of two years. Exhibitions are not limited in respect to the age of candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects for Examination (primary and secondary groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examination will be in (1) Chemistry, including practical work in the laboratory; (2) Physics, viz., Electricity, Heat, Light; (3) Physiology. Candidates will also have the opportunity of being examined in one or more of (4) Geology, (5) Anatomy, (6) Botany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must give notice of the subjects in which they wish to be examined four weeks prior to the Examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of subjects and group requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No candidate will be examined in more than three of these six subjects, whereof one at least must be chosen from the former group (Chemistry, Physics, Physiology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the wish of the master and seniors that excellence in some single department should be specially regarded by the candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: registration before examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must send their names to one of the tutors, Dr. Parkinson, Mr. Bonney, or Mr. Sandys, before the commencement of the Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Examination will commence on Friday, the 13th of December.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to offer for Classical or Mathematical subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may also, if they think fit, offer themselves for examination in any of the Classical or Mathematical subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional option beyond the specified Natural Science subjects; candidates should consider the preference for demonstrating excellence in a single department.
